name: Seeing the Universe Anew: Ideas That Changed Science
description: From the Sun-centred sky of Copernicus to the first ripples of gravitational waves: the discoveries that changed what we know about matter, life, Earth and the cosmos.

checkpoints.name: The Earth moves
checkpoints.note: For nearly two thousand years the Earth sits at the centre of the sky. Aristarchus suggests otherwise, and in 1543 Copernicus publishes a full Sun-centred model that opens the way for the revolution to come.

checkpoints.name: The scientific revolution
checkpoints.note: Galileo turns a telescope to the sky, Kepler finds the shape of orbits, and Newton explains them with one law of gravity and a new kind of mathematics.

checkpoints.name: Matter, life and light
checkpoints.note: Atoms, cells, inherited traits, evolution and the electromagnetic field enter science, though atoms and Mendel's laws win wide acceptance only after 1900. Chemists order the elements, doctors trace disease to germs, and Becquerel finds radioactivity.

checkpoints.name: Relativity, quanta and a growing cosmos
checkpoints.note: Einstein recasts space and time, quantum mechanics describes the atom, and Hubble shows that the universe is expanding, which leads to the idea of a Big Bang.

checkpoints.name: Reading the cosmos and the cell
checkpoints.note: The structure of DNA is solved, the continents are shown to drift and an echo of the Big Bang is heard. The Higgs boson confirms a prediction made in 1964, and gravitational waves confirm a theory a century old.
